QF.id: XIII Trading, Clearing, Settlement and Risk Management_83

question.text: Under SEBI's penalty framework for margin short-collection, if a trading member's shortfall in client margin collection exceeds Rs 10 lakh, the penalty rate is:

answer.text: 1% of the shortfall amount per day
0.5% of the shortfall amount per day
0.1% of the total margin required per day

explanation.text: The Logic: SEBI's margin short-collection penalty regime is conventionally a slab-based structure under which the per-day penalty is computed as a percentage of the actual shortfall amount rather than as a flat fee or as a percentage of the total margin required. Larger shortfalls fall into a higher slab, and the slab for very large shortfalls (above Rs 10 lakh) is set at 1% of the shortfall per day, reflecting the regulator's intent to escalate the penalty as the shortfall grows. The Trap: 0.5% per day belongs to the lower slab for smaller shortfalls, not to the above-Rs-10-lakh slab. The penalty is neither a flat rupee amount nor a fraction of total required margin — it is calculated on the shortfall itself. Note: The specific 1% per-day rate for client margin short-collection above the Rs 10 lakh threshold was not located in the cited workbook pages (IR p.263-p.264 and p.264-p.267; Equity p.163-p.165; Currency p.180-p.183), which describe the short-collection monitoring framework, snapshots, and the existence of penalties in general but not the exact slab rate. The framing above is general Indian-derivative regulatory knowledge rather than a workbook citation.
